subject: ZenithX — k6 load window & SLO clarifications
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@zenithx.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick follow-up from today's SLO discussion

Hi Aisha — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we're all aligned: 

Summary of what we heard from ZenithX:
- Primary SLO: 95th percentile generation latency <= 220ms for standard text generation (context up to 1024 tokens).
- Peak concurrency target: sustained 400 concurrent streams; spiky bursts up to 1,200 for short windows (approx 3–5 minutes).
- Throughput goal: 30k tokens/sec aggregated during peak windows.
- Streaming behavior: client-side expects chunked token streaming with max 150ms gap between chunks for perceived interactivity.

Requests from our side:
1) Please confirm the preferred test windows (UTC times). We proposed a 3-hour window next Tuesday 2027-06-15 16:00–19:00 UTC.
2) We need a list of any IPs that must be allowlisted for the k6 runner and any VPN endpoints you require.
3) Share the representative prompt set and sample payload distribution (we received a basic CSV but would like a richer distribution file for k6).
4) Test accounts: we'll provision temporary API keys and separate test account IDs — can you confirm the max number of parallel test accounts we should create?

Attachments: I've attached a starter k6 script set and an allowlist template; Dylan can tweak k6 ramp patterns based on your prompt distribution.

I'll loop in Dylan for runtime config and Marissa for any billing/limits questions. If the proposed window works, we'll lock it and send final runbook.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: zenithx-k6-scripts-v1.zip (k6 scripts, README)
Attachment: allowlist-request.csv (template)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@zenithx.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: perf-team@zenithx.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ZenithX — k6 load window & SLO clarifications

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming details from our side: 

- 95th p95 target: 220ms is correct for generative endpoints (we will flag any streaming-only endpoints separately).
- Concurrency: 400 sustained, bursts up to 1.2k acceptable. Note: during burst windows, our frontend opens long-poll streaming connections for ~90% of users.
- Throughput: 30k tokens/sec aggregate is a good target.
- Streaming: we need chunk gaps <= 150ms; also please ensure SSE/HTTP2 streaming keeps connection warm for up to 60s idle.

Test windows: Tue 2027-06-15 16:00–19:00 UTC works for us as a primary window; we can also do a backup on Thu 2027-06-17 same time.

Allowlist/IPs: we'll send a CSV with our egress gateway IPs and any VPN endpoints by EOD tomorrow.

Prompt distribution: attaching a richer payload distro and an updated list of end-to-end journeys (see attachment zenithx-test-accounts.csv).

Accounts: please provision up to 800 parallel test accounts — some runners will reuse tokens but we want separate IDs to mirror tenancy.

We also have a security requirement: test traffic must not include PII. Our perf-team will verify sample prompts before the run.

Thanks — Aisha
Head of Platform Operations
ZenithX

Attachment: zenithx-test-accounts.csv (account ids + journey mapping)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@zenithx.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ZenithX — k6 load window & SLO clarifications

Hi all — looping in with engineering notes and what I'll need to finalize the k6 job: 

1) k6 config: please confirm the token size distribution and percentage of streaming vs non-streaming flows. If 90% are streaming, the script will open a WebSocket/HTTP stream per VU and continuously read tokens until the scenario finishes.
2) Ramp pattern: propose 15m ramp to 400 VUs, hold 40m, then spike stage: ramp to 1200 VUs over 60s, hold 5m, then ramp down. We'll run 3 full cycles in the 3-hour window.
3) Data/PII: we'll validate that the provided prompts are PII-free; if any sample fails, we'll replace placeholders. Please mark any prompts that are synthetic.
4) Allowlist: we need allowlisted IPs for the k6 orchestrator (three ranges) and a DNS name if you prefer CNAME-based allowlisting. See allowlist-request.csv for format.

I attached an updated k6 script that supports streaming simulated chunk delays and SSE keepalive. If anything in the prompts requires special header injection (tenant-id, feature flags), include those in the prompt distro file.

I'll also collect baseline telemetry (token/sec, p50/p95/p99, stream chunk gaps) and produce a short runbook we can share post-test.

-Dylan
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: zenithx-k6-scripts-v1.zip (updated with streaming module)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@zenithx.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: perf-team@zenithx.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ZenithX — k6 load window & SLO clarifications

Dylan — thanks. We've annotated the payload distro: field "stream_pct" = 90, average token_length = 48, 10% of requests are long-form (>= 800 tokens).

We've attached an allowlist CSV with our gateway IP ranges and a short list of VPN egress nodes. For CNAME allowlisting we can create a test-dns.zenithx.net record if that simplifies onboarding.

Two security asks: 
- Please confirm you will not log raw prompt text as part of temporary test telemetry (hashes are fine).
- We require a signed NDA addendum for this performance engagement; can your legal send a short addendum?

Aisha

Attachment: allowlist-request.csv (gateway ranges + VPN endpoints)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@zenithx.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ZenithX — k6 load window & SLO clarifications

Hi Aisha — quick note on ops and billing: 

- We can provision temporary test API keys scoped to "perf" with usage caps; please confirm whether you'd like keys per account or shared per-runner.
- For the engagement NDA addendum: legal can do a one-page addendum focused on test telemetry and non-PII logging; Jordan, I'll kick off the doc and loop legal.
- IP allowlist received — ops will push the ranges to the test plane once DNS is confirmed.

I'll send a calendar invite for Tue 2027-06-15 16:00–19:00 UTC and include runbook link once drafted.

Best,
Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: (none)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@zenithx.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ZenithX — k6 load window & SLO clarifications

Aisha — great, thanks for the fast turnaround. Next steps (action items with owners):
- Jordan: finalize calendar invite and send runbook link (today). Runbook will include exact k6 commands, prometheus/trace endpoints, and expected artifact locations.
- Dylan: finalize k6 artifacts and upload zenithx-k6-scripts-v1.zip to the shared drive; ensure streaming module is toggled for 90% flows.
- Marissa: open NDA addendum with legal and provision perf-scoped API keys (up to 800 parallel accounts).
- Aisha/ZenithX: confirm DNS/CNAME for allowlist or provide final IP ranges (EOD Fri 2027-06-11).

If all looks good, we will treat Tue 2027-06-15 as confirmed and perform a short warmup run 30m before the main window. Appreciate the partnership — we'll capture telemetry and a short post-mortem with recommended config changes.

Jordan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
